_readme: Functions granted EXECUTE to `authenticated` that check-dormant-rpcs.mjs must not fail on.
An entry is a debt, not an absolution. The gate exists because this codebase repeatedly shipped
complete server work no button could reach (BACKLOG.md G1-G15). Delete the entry when the caller
lands -- do not delete the entry to make the gate quiet.
THE COUNT WAS WRONG FOUR TIMES, each because this script read SQL badly: it ignored
`drop function`; it treated a migration COMMENT as a call site; and it read line by line, so in a
grant naming several functions only the first line carried the keywords; and it counted a function
named inside a QUOTED STRING as a call -- `issue_certificate`'s only apparent call site in the whole
repository was its own `raise exception` message. 'Zero' was never true.
Of the twenty-one that were real, fifteen have been wired and their entries removed. The four
below are not gaps at all, and saying which kind of not-a-gap each one is was the useful part:
two are superseded predecessors, and two are machine entry points with no human caller by design.

record_resident_service_task.reason: Superseded duplicate write path, and the earlier reason here was wrong. Documenting a service task works: the floor and the task queue both call `record_service_task_response`, which 20260726060100 introduced with a response plus structured `exception_details`, replacing this one's status/note/supervisor_notified model. Unlike `save_report_schedule` this predecessor does NOT delegate -- it is a second full implementation writing the same rows on the older model. Wiring it would be actively wrong. Every way to close it is a deprecation decision with a blast radius outside this repository: revoking the grant gives any external caller a 42501, and making it delegate (the 20260717021844 pattern) would subject existing callers to the successor's per-requirement `acceptable_completion_responses` allowlist, which this one never applied -- `completed_by_other` has no mapping in the successor's `case` at all. The delegating option is probably right and it is still a call to make on data nobody in this repository can see, so it is recorded rather than taken.

save_report_schedule.reason: Superseded compatibility shim, not a missing capability -- and the earlier reason here was wrong. Report scheduling works: the Value Center calls `save_report_schedule_configuration`, which 20260717021844 introduced as a strict superset (delivery hour and minute, day of week, day of month, and a schedule id so an existing schedule can be edited). The same migration re-declared this older signature as a wrapper that delegates with defaults of 07:00, Monday, the 1st. It is dormant by design and wiring it would be wrong -- the richer function is the one a person should reach. Kept rather than dropped because it is granted to `authenticated` and an external integration could still be calling the older signature.

record_regulatory_shadow_run.reason: Machine entry point, not a screen. It takes a rule version, a baseline version, a cohort window, an evaluated count and an engine version -- output from a rule engine running a candidate version alongside the current one, not anything a person types. The differences it produces ARE now actionable: `reconcile_regulatory_shadow_difference` is wired (G15.19). Giving this one a form would be inventing a user for it. What it needs is the engine that calls it, which does not exist in this repository.

record_regulatory_fixture_result.reason: Machine entry point, not a screen. It records one golden-fixture result for a given engine version with a request id -- conformance-harness output. Same reasoning as G15.18: the missing piece is the harness, not a button.

issue_certificate.reason: Superseded compatibility endpoint, and the migration that superseded it says so outright. `20260711154819_atomic_course_completion_certificates.sql` moved issuance inside `complete_course_assignment()` because the two-call browser flow left a valid completion with no certificate whenever a request failed between the calls, and records that this function "remains as an idempotent compatibility endpoint". Its client hook was deleted rather than given a screen: calling it from the product again would mint a certificate with no completion behind it, which is the exact invariant that migration exists to hold. It stays granted because an integration outside this repository could still be calling it. THIS ENTRY IS ALSO THE FOURTH READING BUG'S EVIDENCE -- the function's only apparent call site anywhere was its own error message, `'certificates are not directly writable by clients; use issue_certificate() / service role'`, and the gate counted that string as a caller until `blankSqlStrings` landed.
